name: a whole-line comment is dropped
input:
echo one
# echo two
echo three

name: a TRAILING comment is stripped, not just a whole-line one
a backslash continuation is joined into one logical line
a comment on a continued line does not leak its text into the joined line
a heredoc body is inert data, never a shell statement
input:
cat <<'EOF'
cargo run -- --expect-channel sidecar
EOF
echo after

name: a here-string opens no body and does not swallow the following lines
a quoted # is data, not a comment
a # mid-word does not open a comment
an apostrophe mid-word does not open a quote that swallows a real comment
an escaped quote inside a double-quoted string does not close it early
a # inside a single-quoted string is data
blank lines are dropped
an unquoted heredoc delimiter opens a body too
a dash-heredoc opens a body
a here-string whose word is a quoted LITERAL opens no body either (CPE-1933)
a here-string and a real heredoc on one line: only the heredoc opens a body
input:
echo a <<<"lit" && cat <<EOF
body
EOF
echo after

name: CPE-1936 N8: a heredoc token inside a DOUBLE-quoted string opens no body
input:
echo "use <<EOF to start a heredoc"
cargo run --bin verify-release-artifacts -- --expect-channel sidecar
echo tail

name: CPE-1936 N7: an indented terminator does NOT close a plain <<EOF
input:

  EOF
cargo run --bin verify-release-artifacts -- --expect-channel sidecar
EOF
echo after

name: CPE-1936 N8: a heredoc token inside a SINGLE-quoted string opens no body either

name: CPE-1936 N8 live shape: the GitHub multi-line output idiom is not a heredoc
CPE-1936: a quoted <<TOKEN does not stop a REAL heredoc later on the same line
input:

cargo run -- --expect-channel sidecar
EOF

name: CPE-1936 KNOWN GAP (partially-quoted-delimiter family): a backslash-escaped quote leaves the << UNquoted, so a body IS opened -- but bash's delimiter is EOF-plus-quote, not bare EOF, so closing on bare EOF resumes scanning a body line as code
CPE-1936 N7: <<- DOES tolerate an indented terminator
CPE-1936 N7: a uniformly indented block (a heredoc read out of raw YAML) still closes

          cat > "$notes" <<'EOF'
